2027 Volkswagen T-Roc R Drops Camo at the Nurburgring, Looks Ready for Unveiling
12 photos
Photo: SH Proshots
Teased in November 2025, the upcoming T-Roc R is the whitest crossover at the Nordschleife right now. Caught lapping the German circuit in anger, the compact performance crossover wears little in the way of camouflage over its production-intent body panels. When the Volkswagen Group doesn't even try hiding a yet-unreleased model, that is when you know the debut is right around the corner.
Its thin disguise covers a front end that appears unique to the R, distinct from the R Line that is all show and no extra go. For the series-production spec, Volkswagen is believed to use a lot of black to create the impression of a wider vehicle. A sizable lower intake can also be seen, along with a horizontal bar.
Equipped with 20-inch lightweight wheels, the spied test vehicle is wearing 245-section rubber boots. Just as expected from an R, the brake calipers are painted in the performance sub-brand's trademark blue shade. While on the subject of brakes, the front and rear discs are larger than what you get on the R Line version.
Slotting below the Tiguan, the T-Roc has forever been a pretty good-looking crossover. The R Line is even more, whereas the R brings the point home with a quad-piped Akrapovic titanium exhaust system. Its round outlets are housed within a specific valance panel with a diffuser-like central section. The gloss-black finish of the valance carriers over to the wheel arch cladding and side skirts.
The roof spoiler isn't all that different from the R Line. Actually, it sure looks as if Volkswagen saved a few euros by transplanting it altogether. This restraint fits the R sub-brand's habit of keeping its voice down. From certain angles, you can further see that Volkswagen's latest prototype is running a panoramic glass roof.
Photo: SH Proshots While pics of the interior have yet to be snapped, the 2027 Volkswagen T-Roc R is not going to impress anyone who experienced a 911 GT3. Expect only a bit more sportiness than you get in the R Line, nothing more. Building on lesser versions of the T-Roc , the R makes use of MQB Evo bones, albeit with a big twist.
Said twist concerns the rear axle, which integrates Magna electronically controlled multi-place clutch packs. One takes care of the left wheel, and the other works its magic on the right side. This design allows the electronic brain of the car to actively meter out torque mechanically to either side of the rear axle. Lesser 4MOTION, meanwhile, uses the brakes to slow down the spinning wheel.
Regular all-wheel drive forces equal torque to both sides, while the Torque Splitter of the R directs up to 100 percent of the rear axle's torque to either wheel. This behavior overloads the outside rear wheel during hard cornering to pivot the vehicle, thus fighting understeer in a front-biased vehicle with a higher center of gravity than you get in the Golf R hatchback and its longroof-bodied sib.
Because of the MQB Evo connection to the Golf R twins, the T-Roc R crossover is certain to pack the very same iron-block turbo inline-four mill. In the compact hatchback and wagon, it delivers a mega 333 ps (328 hp) and 420 Nm (310 lb-ft) in European flavor, with maximum torque delivered at 2,100 revs.
A manual isn't going to happen, not when Wolfsburg couldn't make a case for rowing your own in the Golf R. Alas, a dual-clutch box will have to suffice. If the German automaker borrows the DQ381 of the Golf R, then look forward to wet clutches instead of the DQ200's dry clutches. While the dry system is more efficient, its maximum torque capacity isn't good enough for this engine.

Third-Gen Fiat Panda Refuses to Die: Here's a New Pandina Tributo Autobianchi Special Edition
12 photos
Photo: Fiat
Believe it or not, the third generation of the Fiat Panda nameplate has been around since 2011, and a decade and a half later it is not showing any signs of slowing down. Quite the contrary.
The Fiat Panda city car was born in 1980 as a simple, two-box three-door hatchback that was penned by Giorgetto Giugiaro and Aldo Mantovani of Italdesign. The success was legendary, and the original was produced until 2003, for no less than 23 years. The second generation was completely redesigned to bode well for the early 2000s and it lived for less than a decade as the third iteration appeared in 2011 at the Frankfurt Motor Show.
Now, 15 years and many iterations later, the third-generation Fiat Panda has no plans to retire, and the Italian automaker even introduces a new special edition, the fresh Pandina Tributo Autobianchi , set as the new flagship version that also pays homage to “one of the most distinctive names in Italian automotive history.”
The date of its reveal, October 21, 2026, also has a symbolic importance: it connects the past and present because precisely 30 years ago the final Autobianchi Y10 was registered. As a reminder, the Autobianchi Y10, introduced in 1985, was derived from the Fiat Panda platform and reinterpreted “the concept of the compact car through sophisticated styling and refined finishes.”
Now, the new Pandina Tributo Autobianchi, with Pandina being in itself a special version of the Fiat Panda Cross model that pays tribute to the Italian nickname of the car, will stand out with its exclusive perks: an exclusive hue, contrasting black exterior details, dedicated alloy wheels, and various Tributo Autobianchi personalization elements, plus new interior finishes.
More precisely, Fiat’s new Pandina Tributo Autobianchi joins the Pandina range above the Pop, Icon, and Cross trim levels, all available with a hybrid powertrain, wearing a new Platino colour, developed specifically for this version and exclusively available on this special edition. There’s also a contrasting black roof and tailgate, exclusive 15-inch diamond-cut alloy wheels, and more.
Inside, the car has light-sand microfiber seats with a “quadrettoni” pattern and a dedicated logo on the front headrests, plus matching light-sand soft-touch door panel inserts. There’s also a Platino-painted dashboard fascia, dedicated “Tributo Autobianchi” welcome graphics on the instrument cluster and radio, plus bespoke floor mats and other finishes.
The new version will be produced at the Italian plant in Pomigliano d’Arco, and “Pandina Tributo Autobianchi retains all the qualities that have made the model so successful: simplicity, practicality, accessibility and versatility, enriched with a touch of Italian elegance.” Fiat leads the European A segment with the Pandina model, announcing over 100k registrations (86k in Italy) during nine months, up 7% compared to last year.

MINI Australia Honors Six Decades of "Bathurst Glory" With Ultra-Limited Lucky 13 Special Edition
17 photos
Photo: MINI
The premium British automaker MINI has a special treat for the Land Down Under, paying tribute to a historic motorsport victory with a new limited series. You’ll need to hurry, though, as there are only 26 examples up for grabs.
The company recently expanded its Countryman compact crossover SUV range with the introduction of the fresh MINI Countryman Untamed Edition available for both the Countryman S ALL4 and the all-electric MINI Countryman SE ALL4, pairing the intelligent ALL4 all-wheel drive with bespoke exterior and interior details “that give MINI’s largest and most versatile model an adventurous new character.”
Earlier in September and in July, the brand also brought to Australia the expanded the MINI Paul Smith Edition range to include the Cooper 3-Door, 5-Door and Convertible Paul Smith Editions arriving before the end of the year; and they also brought a tribute to the home of the marque with the MINI Cooper Oxford Edition. But that wasn’t the end of the limited series, as it turns out.
The latest one is also the most exclusive, for sure: MINI Australia has unveiled the new Lucky 13 Edition, created exclusively for the Australian market, and limited to just 26 units, with first customer deliveries planned for the first quarter of 2027. Pricing starts from AU$71,990 MRLP, which includes the GST but not also the on-road and delivery costs, and equates to no less than $50,522 at the current exchange rate.
For the massive price, MINI offers a special edition created exclusively for the Australian market and designed to celebrate Bob Holden and Rauno Aaltonen’s historic 1966 Gallaher 500 victory. It pays tribute to the Morris Mini Cooper S that secured “one of Bathurst’s most celebrated results,” and also celebrates MINI’s “enduring connection to motorsport and Bob Holden’s remarkable contribution to Australian racing history.”
The new special edition comes 60 years since the Australian driver Bob Holden and Finnish rally legend Rauno Aaltonen outright won the 1966 Gallaher 500 at Mount Panorama, Bathurst with a Morris Mini Cooper S. 13 was Bob Holden’s lucky number and the MINI Lucky 13 Edition is based on the gasoline-powered MINI John Cooper Works 3-Door, featuring the 2.0-liter inline-four turbo engine and a seven-speed sports dual-clutch transmission and shift paddles.
There are exclusive circular “13” decals, a finish in classic British Racing Green IV, Glazed White roof and mirror caps with white bonnet stripes, plus 18-inch John Cooper Works Rallye Spoke 964 Bicolor wheels in Frozen Midnight Grey along with a set of high-gloss black John Cooper Works elements: front, side-skirt and rear lower winglets, a carbon-fiber JCW tailpipe finisher and red JCW tow strap.
Inside, the MINI Lucky 13 Edition has John Cooper Works seats and steering wheel, an Anthracite headliner, extended ambient lighting, plus heated and electrically adjustable front seats, along with a Harman/Kardon 12-speaker, 365-watt sound system among other things.

BMW M350 xDrive Gets Virtually Redesigned With Angel Eyes, the Digital BMW M3 Also Enters the Chat
9 photos
Photo: Timur Altynbayev / Behance
BMW is in the middle of its largest product offensive in modern times, which kicked off last fall with the launch of the second-gen NA5 BMW iX3 Neue Klasse compact electric crossover SUV. And they are now building an avalanche.
The tidal wave continued this spring with the NA0 battery electric compact executive car – the second-generation BMW i3 – now a sedan of the Neue Klasse clan. These two have all the Neue Klasse assets – outside, inside, and the dedicated EV platform. There’s also the brand-new NA7 first-ever BMW iX4 coupe-SUV, along with a bunch of partial Neue Klasse models that were kept on the enhanced CLAR platform for various reasons.
Those include the mid-cycle refresh of the BMW 7 Series and i7, the all-new BMW X5 (G65), which remained on CLAR to support no less than five different powertrains, or the G50 BMW 3 Series, the eighth generation of the compact executive model. Additional Neue Klasse novelties are coming, like the recently leaked BMW i3 Touring, the spied BMW 5 Series facelift, or the fresh BMW M5 and M3 – the latter set to be offered both with ICE and EV options.
Speaking of the BMW 3 Series and the M3, everyone had something to say about the fresh top-of-the-line M350 xDrive and its exclusive yellow daytime running lights plus the enhanced 3.0-liter B58 turbo inline-six engine that now churns out no less than 437 hp. Naturally, the rumor mill also chipped in, along with the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI – even if some of them did it later than others.
For example, the virtual artist Timur Altynbayev is from Kazakhstan, but his latest unofficial, hypothetical design projects feel targeted at the Bavarian areas of Munich because he’s ready to show us their unofficial, hypothetical design project based on the BMW 3 Series G50, the M350 xDrive in particular.
The pixel master says that he feels like the new BMW 3 Series can easily be reskinned with references to the legendary E30 BMW M3 coupe. So, at the front of the M350 xDrive, he added the Neue Klasse illuminated kidneys from the latest X5 along with dual round LED surround daytime running lights, bringing back the iconic ‘angel eyes’ in a modern manner.
Around the back, he lowered the edge of the trunk line and also made the rear LED clusters “bigger and shorter” to pay a distinctive tribute to the E30 BMW M3. While we’re still on the subject of the M3, by the way, the artist didn’t stop with the M350 xDrive and also imagined a potential Neue Klasse BMW M3 based on the project, with all the front LEDs dressed in yellow and a monster aerodynamic package plus dual central exhausts! NATO will allow Ukraine to buy weapons, ammunition and military equipment via its centralized procurement agency, potentially allowing Kyiv to obtain defense supplies faster and more cheaply, the Financial Times reported on Thursday.
“It provides Ukraine with the ability to have a more structured framework to leverage a broad range of capabilities that we offer: procurement expertise, support services and access to established industrial base,” the NATO Support and Procurement Agency (NSPA) director of support to operations, Jacqueline Borsboom, told the FT.
The deal comes amid worsening U.S.-Ukraine relations since U.S. President Donald Trump announced a diesel export deal with Russia this month to lower U.S. fuel prices.
Ukraine has complained of disruption to some intelligence sharing and its use of the Starshield satellite system, though Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said a meeting in Oslo on Tuesday had agreed to resolve those issues.

Nissan Sentra Gains Midnight Edition for 2027, Here's How Much It Costs North of the US Border
7 photos
Photo: Nissan
After it launched in the United States of America a couple of months ago, the 2027 Nissan Sentra is now officially on sale in Canada, too.
The lineup comprises five different trim levels, including the newly launched Midnight Edition. This model sits at the very top of the family, and replaces the SR Premium grade. The novelties include new 18-inch alloys finished in black, a black two-tone exterior, black trim and badging on the outside, and an available wireless charging pad for more consistent and faster charging, as well as enhanced compatibility.
Pricing for the 2027 Nissan Sentra S starts at CA$28,536 (equal to US$20,300). This model features 16-inch wheels with covers shod in 205/60 all-season tires, a tire repair kit, tire pressure monitoring system, LED headlights and taillights, a glossy black with chrome grille, glossy black side mirror casings with heating, cloth upholstery, manually adjustable front seats, 60/40-split rear seats, and a four-speaker sound system.
Additional highlights include the 7-inch multi-information display, a 12.3-inch touchscreen infotainment system, wireless Android Auto and Apple CarPlay, Google Assistant voice recognition, Siri Eyes Free, Bluetooth, hands-free test messaging assistant, three USB-C ports, and a 12-volt port. The intelligent cruise control, remote keyless entry with push-button ignition, manual air conditioning, active ride control, intelligent ride control, rear door alert, intelligent driver alert, and others are also on deck.
Photo: Nissan From CA$30,536 (US$21,725), the SV version of the 2027 Nissan Sentra becomes available. This model features 16-inch machined aluminum-alloy wheels, body-color door handles, a synthetic leather-wrapped steering wheel with heating, superior cloth upholstery, an enhanced 12.3-inch infotainment system, Nissan Intelligent Key, sun visors with extensions and vanity mirrors, automatic climate control, remote engine start, and a few other bits and bobs.
Nissan’s 2027 Sentra SV Premium kicks off at CA$31,636 ($22,505) and adds heated side mirrors with turn signals, a power tilt/sliding moonroof with a manual sunshade, a wireless charging pad, approach unlock/walk-away lock function for the intelligent key, etc.
The SR grade starts at CA$32,936 (US$23,430), and sports 18-inch alloys shod in 215/45 all-season tires, LED signature headlights, full-width LED taillights, a dark chrome grille, lower body side sill extensions, a rear spoiler, red badging, and a chrome exhaust tip, sport cloth upholstery with accent stitching, a six-speaker sound system, and a few other gizmos.
Last but not least, the 2027 Nissan Sentra family is topped by the SR Premium Midnight Edition, priced from CA$35,666 (US$25,375). The range-topper features black 18-inch alloys, TailorFit sport leatherette upholstery, power-adjustable front seats, a Bose premium sound system with eight speakers, ProPilot Assist, rear sonar sensors, and some extra safety gizmos.
Photo: Nissan Regardless of your trim level selection, all versions of the 2027 Nissan Sentra use the same engine. It is a 2.0-liter DOHC four-cylinder unit that produces 149 horsepower (151 ps/111 kW) at 6,000 rpm) and 146 pound-feet (198 Nm) of torque at 4,000 rpm. The engine can be revved up to 6,600 rpm, and is paired with an Xtronic transmission that channels the power to the front wheels. The CVT is said to have been enhanced for the 2027 model year for a smoother and more linear acceleration profile, as well as crisper acceleration response.
The same lump powers the 2027 Nissan Sentra in our market, too, and in case you forgot, the lineup comprises the S, SV, SR, and SL trim levels. Pricing starts at $22,990 (equal to CA$32,310), $23,990 (CA$33,715), $24,990 (CA$35,125), and $27,990 (CA$39,340), respectively. The Midnight Edition is also available over here, albeit not as a standalone trim level, but as an upgrade package available for the Sentra SR. The bundle, which brings the same goodies, is a $650 (CA$915) option.
Before wrapping it up, we will remind you that the current Nissan Sentra is in the ninth generation. The official unveiling took place a little over one year ago, with the car launching for the 2026 model year initially. Production for North America started in 2025, with the assembly taking place at the Aguascalientes facility in Mexico, and in early 2026, the model also started production in China, at the Guangzhou facility.
Nissan’s latest Sentra is based on the Renault-Nissan CMF-C/D construction, just like its predecessor, as well as the Rogue / X-Trail, old Rogue Sport / Qashqai, Renault Kadjar, Talisman, Megane IV, Koleos II, Scenic IV, Austral, Espace VI, Rafale, Kangoo III, and Mitsubishi Outlander, among others. It is 183.3 inches (4,656 mm) long, 71.5 inches (1,816 mm) wide, and 57 inches (1,448 mm) tall, and has a 106.5 inches (2,705 mm) long wheelbase. The model has a curb weight of over 1.4 metric tons (~3,100+ pounds).
The Nissan Sentra goes up against the likes of the aging Toyota Corolla, as well as the Honda Civic, Kia K4, Mazda3, Volkswagen Jetta, Hyundai Elantra, and other compact sedans, and sits below the Altima in the company’s lineup.

General Motors Is Looking Forward to Engineering the "Intelligence-Defined Vehicle for Everyone"
10 photos
Photo: GM
Yep, General Motors is joining the large pack of automakers that are seeking "a fundamental transformation of our vehicles" as we know them. In other words, they’re trying to ‘reinvent the wheel.’
General Motors, the largest US automaker, usually lets its main brands like Chevy, Buick, Cadillac, and GMC ‘do the talking’ about what’s new and upcoming. Not recently, and not this time around, as they just wrapped up the GM Forward 2026 event.
Sure, there’s also the Cadillac Formula 1 Team, which just designed a custom Texas-themed livery for the upcoming United States Grand Prix, but GM as a whole has been very active thanks to the GM Forward 2026 event, announcing how they are “building toward a future that gives people more capability, more confidence, and ultimately, more time for what matters most:” through a combination of AI, software-defined platforms, intelligent manufacturing, and trusted autonomy, of course.
First and foremost, they will seek to have enterprise AI that helps them reduce development times – up to cutting them in half. GM will seek to significantly lower the traditional four-to-five-year vehicle development timeline, aiming to cutting it in half via enterprise AI and virtualization. More precisely, they will use a unified digital thread from day one to bring together design, engineering, and manufacturing.
For example, their latest advancement in EVs, which focuses on lithium manganese rich battery chemistry, or LMR , was tested virtually on more than 300,000 battery designs before creating a single physical prototype, enabling the team to move from the first LMR battery pack concept to formal program approval in one month!
That’s how we ended up with the Generation 4 platform for mainstream electric vehicles , a unified new architecture that will use LMR battery chemistry for “an exceptional range-to-cost ratio, improved performance, and enhanced durability.” It will also include new propulsion systems that reduce parts count by 40%, as well as a new, central compute and electrical architecture serving as the vehicle’s new foundation with “smarter energy management, seamless software updates, and richer in-cabin experiences.”
The latter next-generation electrical and compute architecture will be decoupled in terms of software relative to hardware, consolidating perception, propulsion, active safety, and chassis controls onto a single, high-speed Central Compute Unit (CCU). It will enable sophisticated in-cabin AI and autonomous driving, both running simultaneously. GM promises 40x more computing power with 30% less wiring length and mass, plus up to 50% faster cellular connectivity than in previous systems.
The platform will debut on the 2028 Cadillac Escalade IQ and then quickly roll out on the company’s “highest-volume gas-powered full-size SUVs and trucks, our three-row crossovers and our fourth-generation electric vehicles,” including the Chevy Silverado.
Meanwhile, OnStar is celebrating its 30th anniversary, and GM’s present for the system is the morphing into a “multimodal intelligence platform” – it is set to become a “connected intelligence layer that will make every drive more personal and enjoyable through AI-powered feature s, while continuing to provide the timely assistance customers trust.”
More precisely, it will be underpinned by the launch of the OnStar AI Assistant in the 2027 Cadillac Lyriq in the coming months through an over-the-air update, with additional GM vehicles to follow later. It will be an AI trained with “GM’s extensive vehicle knowledge,” offering anything from personalized guidance to actual, trusted human support, as well as a new mobile app.
The latter will be the new GM OnStar mobile app, which is set to replace the current OnStar Guardian and Buick, Cadillac, Chevrolet, and GMC vehicle brand apps, striving for a unified experience across vehicles and devices. Additionally, GM announced last year that it is introducing autonomous highway driving starting with the 2028 model year of the Cadillac Escalade IQ.
Now the company said they have started testing pre-production vehicles on closed courses and decided to expand autonomous highway driving to all the “highest-volume, best-selling vehicle lineups, including full-size SUVs and light-duty pickups.”
That means moving beyond EVs to gas-powered vehicles, and to achieve that, they have “hundreds of data-collection vehicles that are driving across the country around the clock, generating approximately 1 million miles of full-rate, multisensory data each month to correlate with and augment a much larger pool of generated data.”

The Fifth-Gen Range Rover Is Getting a Facelift for 2028
14 photos
Photo: SH Proshots
There may be quite a few premium full-size SUVs in today’s automotive world, joined by the usual luxury proposals from Mercedes-Maybach, Bentley, and Rolls-Royce, namely the GLS 680, Bentayga, and Cullinan, but they should all thank the model that initially started this trend a few decades back: the original Range Rover .
As you probably know, the Range Rover Classic hit the assembly line back in 1970 at the Solihull factory in the United Kingdom, and was also made in Australia and Venezuela. Production of this model ceased completely in 1996, and over 326,000 units are said to have been made during this time. Its successor, the second generation, was made between 1994 and 2001 in the UK, and from 2001 to 2012, Land Rover made the L322 generation of the popular SUV.
The L405, which as aged very nicely to be honest, this writer thinks, was made from 2012 to 2021, and one year later, the L460 hit the assembly line. This is the latest generation of the Range Rover , and besides the Solihull factory, it is also put together in India. Gerry McGovern is responsible for the design, and he also left his mark on the 2010 Range Rover, Range Rover Sport, Discover 4, Discovery Sport, and other models over the years, including the latest generation of the iconic Defender.
Now, four years without any serious updates is plenty of time for a vehicle in today’s car world, so it is no wonder that the modern-day Range Rover is now getting a mid-cycle refresh. Land Rover started testing the first prototypes in the open a few months ago, and our spy photographers encountered one of them earlier this week. Fast-forward to present day, and we get to see it again courtesy of a new set of spy shots that just ended up in our inboxes.
Photo: SH Proshots The tester in question had its entire body wrapped in camouflage. Well, save for the pillars, roof, and door mirror casings, because these will carry over with no changes, just like the entire profile, bar the wheels, probably, as we expect the model to get fresh options. After all, it is a mid-cycle refresh that we are talking about, and not an entirely new generation.
However, despite the trippy vinyl stickers, it is clear that the visual updates on the outside are quite modest, to say the least, and chances are that those who are unfamiliar with the design of the current Range Rover will mistake it for the upcoming one. We cannot see and black plastic cladding at the front, aka the fake stuff, and that means that we can see the design of the bumper and grille.
The size and the shape look pretty much the same as before, but we can see that the mesh has been altered and now features smaller horizontal slats that are positioned very close to each other. The headlights look the same as before, but we reckon the daytime running light signature must have been updated. And as far as the front bumper goes, it seems to soldier on from the current model .
Photo: SH Proshots Replacing doors, windows, front fenders, and rear three-quarter panels is pricey, so these are the same. Further back, we can see that the “new” Range Rover still has vertical taillights, though these should be fresh once the model goes official, just like the rear bumper, and the discreet diffuser attached to it.
It is still too early to talk about the interior, because it has yet to open up to the camera. However, reports speak about the facelifted Range Rover perhaps adopting a curved infotainment screen. The digital gauge cluster, steering wheel, trim and upholstery, and other things could also be updated for the facelifted iteration.
Rumor has it that the powertrains will probably carry over unchanged, for the most part, and this means that the BMW-sourced 4.4-liter twin-turbo V8 , featuring mild-hybrid assistance, and delivering up to 607 hp, will still be part of the offering, alongside the inline-six turbocharged 3.0-liter mills, including the PHEVs, and the inline-six diesel for Europe.
Some also believe that the upcoming Range Rover’s chassis could be tweaked with emphasis on making the ride more comfortable. After all, the model still tries to take a swing at the likes of the Mercedes-Maybach GLS 680, Bentley Bentayga, and Rolls-Royce Cullinan, as well as the lesser premium full-size SUVs, and it pretty much bridges the gap between the latter and the former models.
We have yet to learn when Land Rover plans to introduce the facelifted Range Rover , but the updated high-rider might end up sitting under the spotlight officially sometime over the next few months. Chances are that it will reach showrooms across North America for the 2028 model year, with an obvious emphasis on the words “chances are.” What’s your take on the updated Range Rover? Does it look more appealing than the outgoing one, or is the upgrade simply not worth it based on the current information?

No G 63 Pickup From Mercedes-AMG? No Problem With Brabus’ New P 900 Rocket Edition!
126 photos
Photo: Brabus
The three-pointed star brand is finally expanding the new-generation G-Wagen family with a second body style, the Cabriolet , which will join the fixed-roof models from 2028. But is a pickup variant also due? That would be a no, because Mercedes has no intention to turn its popular premium truck into a workhorse.
However, if you really must have such a thing, then you should know that there are several companies out there that would gladly sell you a pickup version of the modern-day G-Wagen. Brabus is one of them, as the famous tuner has been in this game for quite a while now, and their latest project represents their newest take on such a thing.
Christened the Brabus P 900 Rocket Edition, the project was just unveiled, and it is the continuation of the Brabus XLP presented in early 2020. The latest evolution is 211.8 inches (5.35 meters) long, 81.1 inches (2.06 meters) wide, and 80.7 inches (2.05 meters) tall, and the tuner says it is 21.7 inches (68.9 cm) longer than a standard Mercedes-AMG G 63 without the spare wheel mounted at the rear.
This is a true coachbuilt model, as you are looking at a veritable pickup truck. Brabus says the cargo bed is versatile, and has been created by adding a special extension module to the vehicle’s steel ladder frame chassis. The wheelbase has expanded by 19.7 inches (50 cm) compared to the base model, and the rear suspension assemblies have been repositioned rearward by the same distance.
Photo: Brabus A specially manufactured steel bulkhead has been positioned behind the rear seats. The model has a four-door body, and its cargo floor and side-opening tailgate are said to have been made of metal. The bed’s side panels are made of carbon fiber, and the bed also features durable soft-teak decking decorated with red Brabus lettering. Two lockable cargo boxes are also on deck, and they are waterproof.
Brabus’ new P 900 Rocket Edition has been further enhanced with the Widestar widebody kit. It comprises the carbon-exposed fender flares at the front and rear, as well as other enhancements on the outside that further separate this build from the standard Mercedes-AMG G 63. The truck rides on 24-inch Brabus Monoblock II EVO Platinum Edition light-alloy wheels, which have been shod in 295/30 tires at the front, and 345/25 tires at the rear. The Ventus rubber is said to have been developed specifically for these wheels by Hankook.
The Brabus Ride Control aluminum coilover suspension was calibrated specifically for the low-profile rubber, and the truck sits 1.8 inches (45 mm) lower compared to the base model . Illuminated running boards are also on deck, as well as two chrome tailpipes on each side of the vehicle, framed by the exposed-carbon surrounding and featuring ambience light. More carbon fiber is visible at the front and rear, and the special badging contributes to the makeover.
On the inside, the Brabus P 900 Rocket Edition is also on the special side of things, with the pictrued machine featuring soft black leather and Alcantara upholstery with a quilting pattern that can be seen on the seats, door cards, and other parts of the interior. Leather floor mats are also on deck, and so are the leather-wrapped footwells. Red decorative stitching and piping are also included, as well as carbon fiber elements, pedal pads, and other things.
Photo: Brabus The engine’s displacement has been increased from 3,982 cu-cm to 4,407 cu-cm, and the forged pistons, a specially-developed crankshaft, matching high-performance connecting rods, and other features are part of the makeover. The twin-turbos are also new, and the fuel supply system has been upgraded with high-pressure pumps.
Due to this work, as well as other things, the twin-turbo V8 mill now churns out 888 hp (900 ps/662 kW) at 6,200 rpm and 922 lb-ft (1,250 Nm) of torque at 2,900 rpm. In order to protect the drivetrain, the maximum thrust has been limited to 774 lb-ft (1,050 Nm). The vehicle hits 62 mph (100 kph) in 3.7 seconds, and its top speed has been electronically capped at 174 mph (280 kph). Brabus also mentions the custom speedometer, which is calibrated to 186 mph (300 kph).
By comparison, the standard Mercedes-AMG G 63 tops out at 149 mph (240 kph) with the optional AMG Driver’s Package, and hits 62 mph (100 kph) in 4.3 seconds. The bi-turbo 4.0-liter V8 mill steams out 577 hp (585 ps/430 kW) and 627 lb-ft (850 Nm) of torque.
The new Brabus P 900 Rocket Edition is limited to 10 units only, and your pockets must be really deep if you want to own it, because the pictured truck is for sale, and it is listed at 711,718 euros ($799,032) in Germany, excluding VAT. The stock Mercedes-AMG G 63 starts at 192,690.75 euros (equal to $216,330) in its homeland, and $198,750 (equaling 177,005 euros) in the United States of America.

Brepocitinib is on a roll. After winning approval for an autoimmune skin disease, Roivant Sciences subsidiary Priovant’s drug hit all primary and secondary endpoints in a pair of Phase 3 non-infectious uveitis trials, leading analysts to say the candidate “looked superior to Humira.”
Roivant Sciences and subsidiary Priovant’s TYK2/JAK inhibitor brepocitinib—recently approved for an autoimmune skin disease—significantly reduced the need for steroid treatment in patients with non-infectious uveitis in a pair of Phase 3 studies.
The results are a “clean win . . . with much better efficacy than AbbVie’s Humira,” currently the only approved non-steroid treatment for non-infectious uveitis (NIU), Leerink Partners said in a Wednesday afternoon note. Caused by viral, bacterial, fungal or parasitic infection of the uveal tract, NIU can cause pain, redness, photophobia and blindness.
Roivant, which hunts and acquires existing assets to develop on its own, licensed brepocitinib from Pfizer in a joint deal that spun off Priovant in 2022. Priovant gained approval in August for brepocitinib—to be marketed as Lisraya—to treat the autoimmune skin disease dermatomyositis, and the company is now seeking the regulatory go-ahead in NIU based on two identical Phase 3 clinical trials called Clarity-1 and Clarity-2.
Approvals
Priovant nabs first FDA approval for targeted tablet in dermatomyositis
Lisraya carries a boxed warning typical of JAK inhibitors, but otherwise has a broad label that allows use in all adults with the rare autoimmune disease, setting up the drug for blockbuster status in a few years, according to Leerink.
August 28, 2026
·
2 min read
·
Tristan Manalac
Read more
Patients taking brepocitinib in both studies went more than 48 weeks before treatment failure—which captures tolerability and efficacy by measuring the time it takes for patients to stop taking the drug for any reason—compared with just 12 weeks for patients on placebo, meeting the trials’ primary endpoints, Roivant reported on Wednesday. Patients in the treatment arm went 40 weeks without requiring steroids, which set a “new bar” for noninfectious uveitis therapies, according to the company.
Pooled analysis across the Clarity program saw 62% of patients on brepocitinib remain steroid-free at 48 weeks, compared to 20% on placebo.
Leerink noted that 50% of patients fail on Humira within six months. Although the studies did not pit the two drugs against one another, the analysts said that brepocitinib “looked superior to Humira on a cross-trial basis with a much more aggressive steroid tapering schedule.”
Brepocitinib’s effectiveness spanned a number of different patient subgroups, including those with or without experience taking a tumor necrosis factor (TNF) inhibitor such as Humira and those with forms of uveitis including idiopathic disease, the sight-threatening visual condition birdshot chorioretinopathy and the inflammatory disease sarcoidosis.
Brepocitinib also met all of the trials’ secondary endpoints, including measurements of sustained steroid-free disease inactivity, chorioretinal vascular leakage—or the abnormal escape of fluid and plasma from blood vessels into the retina— and patient-reported visual aptitude. The drug candidate also resolved macular edema in 42% of eyes in patients who the condition in addition to uveitis, compared with just 4.8% on placebo.
Only 3% of participants discontinued brepocitinib because of an adverse event, most of which were mild or moderate, according to the company.
“The breadth and magnitude of benefit seen in the Clarity studies position brepocitinib to potentially set a new standard for the treatment of non-infectious uveitis,” Priovant CEO Ben Zimmer said in a prepared statement. “With Lisraya now commercially available for adults with dermatomyositis, we see NIU as the potential next pillar of a leading rare disease immunology franchise.”
Priovant plans to file a supplemental application for the drug in NIU in the first half of 2027. Leerink analysts said Roivant management is exploring a first-line approach for brepocitinib in NIU, particularly as the studies showed largely consistent benefit in patients who had previously taken a TNF inhibitor and those in the overall treatment population.
The analysts have projected sales of $54 million for Lisraya in dermatomyositis, and $559 million in fiscal year 2028. For non-infectious uveitis, the analysts modeled $2.3 billion in unadjusted sales by the end of 2029, skewing higher if the drug receives a label friendly to patients who have not taken a TNF inhibitor like Humira.
Brepocitinib is one leg of a “three-legged stool,” making up the clinical and commercial prospects at the hub-and-spoke pharma conglomerate, Roivant CEO Matt Gline told BioSpace earlier this month. The other two legs are the pulmonary hypertension candidate mosliciguat, which is currently in a late-stage study after succeeding in Phase 2, and a mid- to late-stage anti-inflammatory drug candidate called IMVT-1402.
Gline told BioSpace prior to the readout that he expected the NIU readout to give brepocitinib “another brick to build a big wall.”
